about: Ten quiz answers for the #4673 trial: a sender describing a kind of person, no real names. Fields follow the quiz questions in #4674's comments.

personas.who: my aunt, a retired ER nurse
personas.listens_to: true-crime podcasts and the BBC World Service
personas.dinner: hospital staffing and how much worse it has got since she retired
personas.already_heard: the usual 'nurses are heroes' talk; anything that gets basic medicine wrong
personas.situation: in the kitchen cleaning up after dinner, hands wet, phone on the counter speaker
personas.push: something new where I'd want her thinking
personas.expert: she is the expert; the episode is something we both react to

personas.who: a coworker who just moved here from a farm town
personas.listens_to: agriculture news and old-time radio dramas
personas.dinner: why grocery prices don't match what farmers get paid
personas.already_heard: the 'small farms good, big farms bad' argument
personas.situation: on a long walk with headphones

personas.who: my teenage nephew who is into robotics club
personas.listens_to: YouTube engineering channels, almost no podcasts
personas.dinner: whether AI will take the jobs he wants
personas.situation: in the car on the way to school, shared speaker with his mom
personas.expert: the host is the expert, but he should feel he can argue back

personas.who: a friend who is a public-school music teacher
personas.dinner: kids learning instruments versus learning on apps
personas.situation: on the couch with coffee on a Sunday
personas.push: something new where I'd want her thinking

personas.who: my dad, a retired civil engineer
personas.listens_to: history podcasts and anything about bridges, dams and infrastructure
personas.dinner: why big public projects take so long and cost so much
personas.already_heard: complaints about regulations with no detail
personas.expert: he is the expert; I want him to tell me what the host got wrong

personas.who: a neighbour who runs a small bakery
personas.listens_to: business interview podcasts and food shows
personas.dinner: how hard it is to hire and keep staff
personas.situation: early morning while baking, speaker on a shelf, hands covered in flour
personas.push: something new where I'd want her thinking

personas.who: a college friend who works as a software engineer
personas.dinner: whether remote work is good for junior people
personas.situation: on the train commute with headphones
personas.expert: both of us know the topic; I want us to disagree usefully

personas.who: my grandmother, who gardens every day
personas.listens_to: gardening radio call-in shows and audiobooks of mysteries
personas.dinner: the weather getting stranger and what grows now that didn't before
personas.situation: in the garden, phone in an apron pocket on speaker

personas.who: a friend who is a public defender
personas.listens_to: legal podcasts and long-form journalism shows
personas.dinner: bail, plea deals and how little time each case gets
personas.already_heard: true-crime that glamorises prosecutors; any host who gets procedure wrong
personas.push: something new where I'd want their thinking

personas.who: my sister, a new parent on leave
personas.listens_to: parenting podcasts and comedy interview shows
personas.dinner: sleep, screen time, and whether all the parenting advice contradicts itself
personas.situation: pushing a stroller around the park, one earbud in
personas.expert: she is the expert; she has read everything
